_comment: phase_thresholds feed WIGame's LOOPING clock (#359): cycle = 2*night, dusk band = night-dusk. Lighting language stated in docs/CHOICE-LOG.md, enforced by scripts/data_lint.py (check_moods). SEALED vs SKY = this file's `day == dusk` pin, an authored call.

rags_camp._comment: Sheltered hollow. `camp_fire_pit` carries the firelight the old card faked in the grade.

sewers._comment: MEASURED, not felt: 0.24/0.26/0.37 + vignette 0.48 read 21 mean, 93% under lum 20 -- a black screen. Cave art is dark alone, so grade carries it: ~2.6x, vignette 0.36 -> 54 mean. deep_tunnels keeps the darkest pin. Other half of the cure = three decor phosphor lights, so the south is not void.

inn_player_room._comment: #350: inn's own day/dusk/night ladder, not the corridor pin; sconce = dusk/night warmth; window daylight, no lights_by_day.

inn_upstairs._comment: TIME-INVARIANT: a corridor lit by its own sconce. `window_blue` decor is dressing, not a light well.

barracks._comment: TIME-INVARIANT (inn_upstairs precedent): staffed day and night, so it never tracks the outside clock.

runners_guild._comment: TIME-INVARIANT (barracks/inn_upstairs precedent): couriers keep counter hours, so the room reads the same at any phase.

ruin_surface._comment: Vignette between floodplains (0.4) and sewers (0.45) -- exposed but ruined, not oppressive.

deep_tunnels._comment: The Raskghar descent: DARKEST pin in the game, time-invariant -- no daylight reaches it.

riverfarm_village._comment: "harvest light" -- the ONLY map whose day grade tips warm; deep-blue night per spec sec.1.

witch_hollow._comment: "green shade" -- never identity white even at day (canopy); dusk is the home key (firefly-dense); vignette 0.50 = enclosure without an underground pin.

mercantile_alleys._comment: Hedault's bench: night read 22 mean, floor/wall/enchanter indistinguishable, half the next-darkest scene. Lifted to the boulevard family; still the darkest Invrisil exterior.

brothers_parlor._comment: The hero-light-over-the-card-table contrast survives the lift (the table light's own energy was raised 0.9->1.0 in the same fix, mercantile decor entry).

stationer._comment: Paper-warm and a shade cooler than the parlor: lamplight on rag paper, not on brandy.

adventurers_rest._comment: Common-hall amber, one notch under the inn's: a bigger hearth in a smaller room.

dungeon_approach._comment: Per-prop accents (trap tells, rubble) ride decor `tint` over this base grade, never a second card. Base lifted ~35% after vault shots read near-black.

trapped_halls._comment: GH-VISUAL-LOG 2026-07-17: base grade lifted ~35% total (12% then a further 20% on user call) (user-ratified USER-EYES item -- vault shots read near-black).

seal_vault._comment: Act V. Brighter/warmer than trapped_halls (0.282): this chamber never fell in; at 0.335 it still read near-black. Tilt is COOL -- ward-light, not a window. `lights_by_day` opts out of day=0.0: a sealed chamber has no sky, so zeroing its lights deleted its only source.

pallass_market._comment: Crystal lamps (steady white #E9EEF2 PointLight2D per-entity) carry the after-dark read; NEVER amber (the standing quarantine check every future screenshot of this map must pass).

pallass_forge._comment: NEUTRAL on purpose: RULE 2 bars a warm grade, not a cold one, and the first cut read colder than the sewers.

pallass_forge_hall._comment: Neutralised with its pallass_forge twin, hue-only at the value it already had.

garden_sanctuary._comment: If the screen never dims and never vignettes here, you are in the garden.

riverfarm_longhouse._comment: Windowless hall, so SEALED: a day-identity pin reads as a SKY and dark-ends its hearth at noon.

sewers_nest._comment: Lockstep with `moods.sewers` DAY (phase-invariant): the nest reads as the underground walked through, not a lit-back-up board. No lights here, so grade is the whole read.

vault._comment: GH-VISUAL-LOG 2026-07-17: grade lifted ~35% total (12% then a further 20% on user call) with the field cards (user-ratified).

trapped_halls_snare._comment: GH-VISUAL-LOG 2026-07-17: grade lifted ~35% total (12% then a further 20% on user call) with the field cards (user-ratified).
